comments.text: Im only 1:25 in, and I feel the need to post. I was raised in the Berkeley/Oakland area of California from the late 70's up to the present. The Black Panther party originated in Oakland but had chapters all over this country, and the BPP legacy is still a powerful one in this community. I benefited as a child, and my child benefited from the free breakfast and lunch programs initiated by the Black Panther Party. Im saddened by the fact that our current government wants to slash these programs completely. If the BPP, a community grassroots movement, could achieve what they achieved, then by no means are we helpless today. Gather as a community, educate yourself on what's happening, and protect our most vulnerable, i.e., our children, our elderly, our veterans, and the immigrant and migrant workers that are a part of our communities. The BPP is a reminder from our not so distant past that great things can be achieved by a community of people on a national level. Now, let's do it on a global level.

Most of breakfast consumed in America was meant for like the onthe-go family. But with that came, you know, crappy food. Like Pop-Tarts had tons of sugar and preservatives in them. And that's where the Black Panther Party comes in. I know it feels random, kind of like out of nowhere, but just like follow me because it's pretty wild. So, the Black Panther Party was a political group who fought for civil rights in the United States. They fought against police brutality and the unfair treatment of black Americans. Many families didn't have means or access to food, especially like breakfast. And a lot of kids in lower inome neighborhoods would go to school without eating anything. So, this like affected how they did in school. I mean, they didn't have enough energy to make it through the day. So, what do you do?
